decisive_items: a well-circumscribed, 11.8 cm cystic mass in the pancreatic head, without invasion of adjacent organs or lymphadenopathy
serum CA 19-9 level was within the normal range
no history of alcohol use, abdominal trauma, or pancreatitis
response.rationale: The vignette describes a benign-appearing, well-circumscribed pancreatic head cyst in an older woman with normal CA19-9 and no pancreatitis history, classic for serous cystadenoma. R8 is a less specific synonym, while R6C is overly broad. Other cystic neoplasms (MCN, IPMN) typically have different demographics or features; pseudocyst and chronic pancreatitis are excluded by history.

rejected.why: Overly broad 'pancreatic cystic neoplasm' without specifying the benign serous subtype; less precise than R4.
Pseudocyst requires prior pancreatitis or trauma, explicitly absent.
Same entity as R4 but less specific label; acceptable runner-up.
Thrombocytosis is a paraneoplastic finding, not the primary diagnosis; the pancreatic cyst is the key lesion.
MCN typically occurs in body/tail and often has ovarian stroma; head location and benign features favor serous cystadenoma.
Chronic pancreatitis contradicted by no history of pancreatitis and imaging showing a cystic mass without ductal changes.
Too nonspecific; does not address the pancreatic cystic lesion.
IPMN usually involves main duct communication and mucin production; not supported by imaging or labs.
